text: The Patriots' 29-26 upset victory over the Bills at Highmark Stadium in Week 4 sent shockwaves through the NFL conversation, with Drake Maye engineering a clutch game-winning drive that proved critical for coach Mike Vrabel's defending AFC champions, making New England the first team to win in Buffalo's new stadium. Maye's performance was particularly notable given his rough early-season slide—he threw three touchdown passes despite committing two turnovers, demonstrating that he didn't need to be perfect to elevate his team when it mattered most. The win has sparked considerable debate about whether early overreactions to the Patriots and other Week 4 winners are warranted or whether we're getting ahead of ourselves in judging their trajectories, though the victory certainly signals the team is capable of competing in a tight AFC East race. The Patriots' roster benefited from the return of all six questionable players, including defensive end Dre'Mont Jones, tackle Craig Woodson, and tight end Eli Raridon, providing Vrabel full availability heading into their divisional matchup.
